I kinda feel it would be nice to rename `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` to just `ExecutionEnvelope` it cuts down on a lot of verbosity `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` -> `SignedExecutionEnvelope` `process_execution_payload_envelope()` -> `process_execution_envelope()` Epbs breakout 10 notes: https://hackmd.io/@ttsao/epbs-breakout-10 anyway temperature check for rename: `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` -> `SignedExecutionEnvelope` `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` -> `ExecutionEnvelope` `process_execution_payload_envelope()` -> `process_execution_envelope()` 👍 = yes 👎 = no 🤷 = **No Opinion** I'm willing to make the PR for this if people want I like those, but for context, when we first started working on ePBS, I made similar suggestions. The takeaway was to wait for renaming until the end, as naming is subjective and highly opinionated among core devs, and we should change it only once. If this is something we are comfortable doing now, then I say go for it https://hackmd.io/@potuz/r1U45HEAR As promissed Wouldn't we achieve the same effect by just saying that any naming is subject to change? I'm not married to any names currently, I just want to have a sane default for now. Ya those sound good for sane defualt A few more... (optional) - Enable more sufficient per builder circuit breaker which lead to less missing blocks if a builder is at fault. Ex: bloxroute incident - Raise floor for balance auction (not sure how to phrase it better but you get the idea) There's an issue in [`validator.md`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7732/validator.md#constructing-a-payload-attestation) > the validator should prepare a `PayloadAttestationMessage` for the current slot, according to the logic in `get_payload_attestation_message` below the function below is `get_payload_attestation_message_signature()` and it returns a `BLSSignature`, not a `PayloadAttestationMessage` Oh yeah forgot that indeed thanks was there supposed to be a `get_payload_attestation_message()` function as well? I don't see that anywhere This sentence: > Set payload_attestation_message.validator_index = validator_index where validator_index is the validator chosen to submit. could also use more clarity since there are 3 validators involved here (`proposer`, `builder`, `ptc attester`) and although I believe you mean the `builder` it's not clear in the sentence i actually still need to pick your brain a bit on this <@755590043632140352> The validator index is for the PTC attester So by "submit" you meant submit the PTC attestation, not the block, or the payload. Ya. Sorry if it's not clear. Open for feedback / PR on how to word it better i think it would be much more clear as: > where `validator_index` is the validator signing the `PayloadAttestationMessage` i had assumed that wasn't the case because of aggregation but i see it's outside of the root that's being signed now there's something very important here that is (from what I can tell) missing from the spec and *might* not be explictly stated in the the docs either and that is the definition of `seen` we have other messages with the same language don't we? maybe we do - not sure Attestation is exactly like this no? > Set data.payload_status as follows > If a SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope has been **seen** referencing the block data.beacon_block_root and the envelope has payload_withheld = False, set to PAYLOAD_PRESENT. > If a SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope has been **seen** referencing the block data.beacon_block_root and the envelope has payload_withheld = True, set to PAYLOAD_WITHHELD. > If no SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope has been **seen** referencing the block data.beacon_block_root set to PAYLOAD_ABSENT. i got on this question because your writeup about the extra time afforded to validators but i'm *inferring* that this must imply that **seen** does **not** mean a payload has successfully been processed by `on_execution_payload()` without returning an error? or is that what you mean by **seen**? that's correct, `seen` here means it is available but not yet verifeid is *ok* But there's still *some* validations performed on the `SignedExecutionPayload` right? are those *just* the gossip validation rules of the `execution_payload` topic? Just gossip validation rules okay that makes sense then, and if we use the same language for regular attestations (seen = passes the gossip validation rules) then this is just my ignorence of the conventions of the spec Oh no, it definitely can be cleaner. Potuz and I probably assume more prior context from the readers. Very grateful for feedback like this So the DA problem with block auctions is funny. Because we don't actually have to keep the invalid payloads around forever.. but we would need to propagate them just long enough for the PTC to attest.. but I guess that's still a DA problem
